notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass on 2026-08-28 under the current durable repository rubric. docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, and radar/inbox/README.md were re-read before searching or grading. Current ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, Yamamoto-schedule, Space M&A and Japanese-jazz searches did not produce a new unrecorded verified Tsuyoshi Yamamoto appearance. The broader US-corridor scan found two unrecorded Dizzy's Club candidates. Admission and priority were decided separately. Saxophone Colossus clears RADAR admission because the specific multigenerational four-saxophone lineup turns Sonny Rollins' improvisational legacy into an instrument-centered live conversation; it is A because the tribute is useful and compelling if New York is already in play, but it does not demand a dedicated regional trip. Gaia Wilmer Large Ensemble featuring Mônica Salmaso clears admission because the engagement is the live album-release realization of a new large-ensemble recomposition of Gilberto Gil's music, combining Brazilian rhythmic language, horn writing and Salmaso's voice; it is A+ because the new project and live setting merit actively making room within a New York trip. Three nights and six sets, plus the project's ongoing multi-volume nature, remove any scarcity-tier case. Batch distribution: A 1 / A+ 1 / S 0 / S+ 0, consistent with the repo's broad-base hierarchy without using distribution as a quota.

events.category: Multigenerational saxophone tribute / Sonny Rollins repertory
events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Saxophone Colossus: Celebrating Sonny Rollins at Dizzy's Club on Thursday, September 10, 2026, with sets at 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM. JALC describes the program as a multigenerational celebration of Rollins' improvisational legacy, with four announced saxophonists — Melissa Aldana, Jerry Weldon, Chris Lewis and Jacob Chung — under the musical direction of pianist Luther Allison, joined by Jared Beckstead-Craan on bass and Anwar Marshall on drums. The official event page states that the ensemble will perform music inspired by Rollins' contributions to jazz; no additional repertoire is inferred.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to hear this is the saxophone conversation, not tribute prestige. Aldana, Weldon, Lewis and Chung bring different generations and different relationships to time, tone and melodic development into the same front line, with Allison directing a rhythm section built to leave room for improvisation. Rollins' language becomes a live point of departure rather than a museum object.
en.trip_verdict: Worth catching if New York is already in play on September 10, especially if the trip can connect to other strong jazz dates that weekend. I would not build a dedicated DMV-to-NYC trip around this program alone.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para escuchar esta noche está en la conversación entre saxofones, no en el prestigio del homenaje. Aldana, Weldon, Lewis y Chung ponen generaciones distintas y distintas maneras de trabajar tiempo, sonido y desarrollo melódico dentro de una misma línea frontal, con Allison dirigiendo una sección rítmica pensada para dejar espacio a la improvisación. El lenguaje de Rollins funciona como punto de partida vivo, no como pieza de museo.
es.trip_verdict: Vale entrarle si Nueva York ya está en juego el 10 de septiembre, sobre todo si el viaje puede conectarse con otras fechas fuertes de jazz ese fin de semana. No armaría un viaje dedicado DMV–NYC únicamente alrededor de este programa.

events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Gaia Wilmer Large Ensemble featuring Mônica Salmaso: Reflections on Gilberto Gil at Dizzy's Club from Friday, September 11 through Sunday, September 13, 2026. Friday and Saturday have 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM sets; Sunday has 5:00 PM and 7:30 PM sets. JALC frames the engagement as an album release celebration honoring Gilberto Gil, with Wilmer reimagining Gil's songs through a large jazz ensemble, Brazilian rhythms, horn arrangements and Salmaso's vocals. The current JALC performance-lineup section names Wilmer as arranger/composer/conductor and Salmaso as vocalist but does not yet publish the individual supporting large-ensemble personnel, so no recording personnel are copied into the live lineup. Apple Music lists Parabólico: Reflections on Gilberto Gil (feat. Mônica Salmaso) by Gaia Wilmer and Gaia Wilmer Large Ensemble as a seven-track, 58-minute Sunnyside Records release dated August 14, 2026.

en.why_it_matters: This is more than a Gilberto Gil songbook night. Wilmer has built a new large-ensemble language around the material, using Brazilian rhythmic cells, extended horn color and Salmaso's unusually precise phrasing to move the songs between MPB memory and contemporary jazz orchestration. Hearing the freshly released project opened up across a working big ensemble is exactly the kind of cultural translation that earns a place on RADAR.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the six sets if a New York trip overlaps September 11-13. It can anchor a strong evening in the city and pairs naturally with other jazz around the weekend, while three nights give enough flexibility that the trip does not need to revolve around a single scarce performance.

es.why_it_matters: Esto es bastante más que una noche de canciones de Gilberto Gil. Wilmer construyó un lenguaje nuevo de gran ensamble alrededor del repertorio, usando células rítmicas brasileñas, color extendido de metales y el fraseo extraordinariamente preciso de Salmaso para mover las canciones entre la memoria de la MPB y la orquestación del jazz contemporáneo. Escuchar el proyecto recién publicado abierto sobre un ensamble grande en vivo es justo el tipo de traducción cultural que merece entrar al RADAR.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets si un viaje a Nueva York coincide con el 11–13 de septiembre. Puede anclar muy bien una noche en la ciudad y combinarse naturalmente con otras fechas de jazz del fin de semana, mientras las tres noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para que el viaje no dependa de una sola función escasa.
